title: The Artificial Intelligence Robot for Cement Testing
summary: The acting director of Dubai Central Laboratory said that its robotic X-ray fluorescence (XRF) system cut cement tests from four days to eight minutes.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: On 16 August 2023 the Dubai Media Office announced that the Dubai Central Laboratory was using robots with X-ray and AI technology to test cement and other construction materials. The acting director of the laboratory said that tests that took four days now took eight minutes. The acting director also said that daily samples rose by 650 percent. In June 2025 Dubai Municipality reported that its robotic X-ray fluorescence (XRF) system was still active. The municipality reported that the system automates the preparation and analysis of cement samples and reduces manual work. It planned to extend automation to tests of concrete, asphalt and soil. No independent source verifies these gains. No source measures a gain in staff safety.
purpose: Automate cement testing and reduce direct handling of hazardous materials.
location: Dubai project; manufacturing-facility implementation location unspecified

ratings.reason: Dubai Municipality reports that cement tests that took four days now take eight minutes, and that daily samples rose by 650 percent. These figures describe time saved and throughput, and no source reports a change in test quality or in construction outcomes.
Lower exposure of staff to hazardous materials is intended. No source gives a measured exposure or health result.
